record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.original_question: Fix r ∈ N ∪ {∞} and k ∈ N, and let D_k^r be the class of C^r self-maps f:R^k→R^k with positive Jacobian determinant everywhere. Determine whether every f in D_k^r can be represented as a finite composition of squares of maps from the same class, that is, whether there exist n and φ_1,...,φ_n in D_k^r such that f = φ_1^2 ◦ ··· ◦ φ_n^2. The paper states that this is solved positively for k=1 but remains open for k>1.

evidence.quote: The problem reads as follows. Let f ∈ Dr_k. Does there exist an n ∈ N and ϕ1,... ,ϕn ∈ Dr_k such that f = ϕ2_1 ◦ ... ◦ ϕ2_n. For k = 1 this problem was solved (positively, n = 4 is enough) by M. Kuczma [149]. For k > 1 it is still open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix $r \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $k \ge 2$. Let $D_k^r$ denote the class of $C^r$ self-maps $f:\mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^k$ whose Jacobian determinant is strictly positive at every point of $\mathbb{R}^k$. For $\varphi \in D_k^r$, write $\varphi^2 := \varphi \circ \varphi$. Determine whether every $f \in D_k^r$ can be represented as a finite composition of squares of elements of $D_k^r$: that is, whether there exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\varphi_1, \ldots, \varphi_n \in D_k^r$ such that
$$f = \varphi_1^2 \circ \varphi_2^2 \circ \cdots \circ \varphi_n^2.$$
(For $k = 1$ it is known that every such $f$ admits a representation as a composition of $n = 4$ squares.)
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return direct evidence of a resolution of this problem for $k > 1$. The available statement of the question reports a positive solution for $k = 1$ (with four squares sufficing) and indicates that the higher-dimensional case remains unresolved. No source contradicting this was located.

status_evidence.title: Diffeomorphism - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General background on diffeomorphisms and their composition.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the squares-composition problem in dimension >1 is reported in standard references.
